title: Ang 435–461: Asa chhants
tomorrow: what could be darker than a night with a hundred moons?

cards: Every family wedding has its songs: the ones the aunties sing late at night, the ones the whole room knows the chorus to. On ang 435 the Granth turns to songs that sound like that: the chhants of Raag Asa. A bride.
A beloved. Youth, waiting, a house to come home to. They are wedding songs, and the beloved in them is the One.

teach.b: A chhant is a song form, and Guru Nanak's chhant on ang 436 rings each line out on a long word at the end, raam, almost like a held note.
It opens, in paraphrase: young bride, in the bloom of youth, my Beloved is full of joy.
The soul is the bride. The One is the groom. All the longing of a wedding, the waiting, the getting ready, the moment of meeting, becomes a picture of the soul and the One.
That's why the Granth sounds so at home at a Sikh wedding.

teach.h: THE SAME PICTURE AS THE LAVAN.
teach.b: The Lavan, the four rounds from last week, use the same picture: the couple walks around the Guru Granth Sahib, and the hymns sing of two people and of the soul and the One, at once.
And in these songs, every listener is the bride. Married or not, any age, a man or a woman.
The union they sing about is open to everyone in the room, including the guest from another faith sitting on the floor near the back.

how: The Asa chhants are read in order and sung as kirtan, and bridal hymns like them are sung at Sikh weddings alongside the four Lavan; guests of any background are welcome to sit with the sangat, heads covered, and share the langar.

s: at a Sikh wedding, the hymns are only about the couple
the Lavan and the chhants use the bride and groom to sing of the soul and the One.
in the chhants, every listener can be the bride, man or woman
the bride is the soul, whoever is listening.
Guru Nanak's chhant on ang 436 is addressed to a young bride
young bride, in the bloom of youth, my Beloved is full of joy.

games.q: your friend from another faith comes to a Sikh wedding and whispers: is it okay if I hum along? what fits the chhants?
o: yes: the songs of union are open to everyone in the room.
no: only the couple's families should sing these.
only once she can read Gurmukhi perfectly.
games.why: in the chhants every listener is the bride, and the union they sing of is open to everyone sitting in the sangat.

practice: If you can, listen to a recording of a chhant from Raag Asa, or read the one on ang 436 aloud, letting the last word of each line ring out. Then hum one long, low note as you breathe out, and let it fade.
Do that a few times, slowly, and notice where the sound sits in your chest.
